texts: Small AP windows may be asymptomatic: B.
An aortopulmonary window is a hole between the ascending aorta and the main pulmonary artery, just above the two valves; the shunt is left to right, like a large PDA or truncus.
Most windows are large: as pulmonary vascular resistance falls in the first weeks, the flow to the lungs rises and heart failure follows, and pulmonary vascular disease can develop early.
So a window is closed when it is found, whatever the age.
In the picture, the sailor by the tiny porthole is calm, while the big porthole floods the money pipe once its wooden blocks fall away.
Memory hook: a tiny porthole, a quiet sailor.
